Issued at 213 PM CST Thu Nov 12 2026

A broad upper trough continues to spiral over the Great Lakes 
this afternoon which has been leading to mostly to completely 
cloudy skies areawide and some lake effect showers in northwest 
IN. The trough has also been advecting in cooler air on blustery
north- northwest winds that have been gusting around 30-40 mph.
While the strongest gusts are expected to diminish after 
sunset, 20-30 mph gusts will persist through Friday as the area 
remains sandwiched between a 1030 mb high near Hudson Bay and a 
997 mb surface low off the eastern CONUS. Temperatures will also
remain seasonably cool through Saturday with daily highs in the
lower 40s and overnight lows in the mid to upper 20s inland and
lower to mid-30s near the lake. 

The main weather concern with this trough will be the 
aforementioned lake effect showers. While the lake effect rain 
showers continue to mainly impact portions of Porter and LaPorte
Counties in IN, recent radar trends are showing the middle part
of the band over central Lake Michigan starting to pivot 
westward towards IL. This trend will continue through the 
evening and will allow the lake effect rain showers to pivot 
into far northeast IL after 4-5 PM CST and persist through most 
of the night. As the band moves into northeast IL the lake 
induced instability is expected to increase as warm lake 
temperatures and the colder air aloft generate equilibrium 
levels around 10000-12000 ft. These ELs are deep enough to allow
the moisture to get into the dendritic growth region and will 
likely start to transition some of the lake effect rain showers 
into a rain/snow mix after sunset. Initially, this mixed 
precipitation wont cause many impacts, but as surface 
temperatures continue to cool into the lower to mid-30s this 
wintry mix should transition over to all snow after midnight 
especially beneath the heart of the band. Given the stout lake 
induced instability snow rates beneath the band could near 1 
inch/hour for a period which may be sufficient for the snow to 
overwhelm the otherwise marginal surface temperatures. 

Now where exactly these highest snow rates setup overnight 
remains somewhat unclear at this time, however, guidance has 
been favoring areas near and along the IL-IN state line. 
Regardless of where the highest snow rates and duration overlap,
pockets of localized snow accumulations of 3-4+ inches continue
to look possible away from Lake Michigan particularly on grassy
and elevated surfaces. For those closer to Lake Michigan and 
not under the core of the band, snow accumulations look to be 
limited in the dusting to maybe a couple tenths range, again 
mainly on grassy/colder surfaces. Couple the potential for these
locally higher snow amounts to occur around the Friday morning 
commute some travel impacts may be seen. Therefore, we have 
opted to extend the Winter Weather Advisory into southern Cook 
and eastern Will counties and maintained it for Lake County, IN 
to highlight this threat. 

Lake effect snow will transition back into a rain by Friday 
afternoon as temperatures warm into the upper 30s and lower 40s 
which should prevent additional accumulations at least through 
the daytime hours. While the lake effect band should begin to 
drift back east Friday afternoon, latest guidance trends show 
this shift being much slower than originally forecast so there 
is a chance the band hovers around the IL-IN state line into 
Friday evening before moving east. Temperatures will once again 
cool into the lower to mid-30s Friday night beneath the band 
which will likely lead to another transition from rain to snow. 
However, with lake induced instability expected to be 
diminishing by this point (ELs around 7000-8000 ft at best) the 
snow rates should be more muted and struggle to overcome the 
surface temperatures. So while some minor (dusting to 0.2 inch) 
accumulations may occur on grassy surfaces in northwest IN 
Friday night, little to no impacts to travel are expected. 

The lake effect showers will taper from west to east across 
northwest and northern IN Saturday morning leaving us with dry 
conditions through at least the middle of next week as a surface
high builds into the region. Temperatures will also begin to 
rebound next week as winds turn southerly resulting in highs in 
the 50s and nighttime lows in the 30s to around 40 for the early
to middle part of the week.

Yack
